turns.t: Come in, Mr Subramaniam. The booking says, cough since you painted the house. Is that right?
Yes, doctor, the cough since we painted the house. We did the whole house, you know. Every room. My son-in-law said, Appa, hire a painter, but I said, why pay?
I see. And the cough began when?
About three weeks back. Starting the second day of painting, it began. And it will not leave me.
Is it worse at any particular time?
Worse near the paint fumes, even now. Yesterday I went to the garage, where the old tins are, and I coughed for ten minutes.
Dry cough, or are you bringing up phlegm?
Dry mostly. My wife says it sounds like a dog, ha ha. She is very kind like that.
Anything else started along with it?
Sneezing, in the first week. A lot. But that has gone now, the sneezing is gone after we opened all the windows.
Good. So the cough remains, the sneezing is gone. Now, you are a known asthmatic?
Yes, asthma since childhood. Also sinus problem, from my thirties. Both, I am carrying for years.
And your inhaler, which one are you using?
Budesonide, the brown one. The dose, I think 200 micrograms, maybe? Twice a day. The pharmacist knows better than me.
We'll confirm with the pharmacy. Any asthma in the family?
My mother had it badly. In her last years, she was always using the pump.
Thank you. And you worked in what field, before retirement?
Bank manager, thirty-two years. Retired now. My granddaughter says I only watch cricket.
Fair enough. Let me take your readings.
Blood pressure 130 over 84. Pulse 82. Temperature 36.8. Oxygen 96 percent. Breathing rate 18.
All okay? I check my pressure at home also, with the machine my son bought.
Yes, all within range. Let me listen to your chest. Deep breaths, mouth open.
There is a slight wheeze when you breathe out, mainly at the bases.
Yes, I can hear it a little myself. Like a small whistle.
My impression is that the paint fumes irritated your lungs, so this is most likely an asthma flare.
So the paint was the culprit. I told my wife.
Likely, yes. I would like to order a lung function test, so we can see how your airways are working now.
Which test is that? The one where we blow into a tube?
Exactly that. Blowing hard into a machine, three attempts. Takes ten minutes, at the front clinic.
No problem. I am free today.
Good. Now, your options for the cough itself. One, keep the windows open and stay away from the garage and the old tins.
Garage, yes. I will tell my son to clear it.
Two, use your budesonide regularly, morning and evening, even when you feel fine.
I sometimes skip when feeling fine. I will not skip now.
Three, let the house air out for another week or two before spending long hours in the freshly painted rooms.
My wife wants to sleep in the guest room anyway, because of the smell. So that works.
Ha. Then four, a damp cloth rather than a dry broom for dust. That is all I need from you.
Understood, doctor. Thank you for the options. I will do one, two, three, and four.
Good. The nurse will take you to the test room. Take care, Mr Subramaniam.
